headline: Isaias Kills Four After U.S. Gulf Landfall; Oil Exchange Authorized
seoTitle: Isaias Kills Four; U.S. Authorizes Emergency Oil Exchange
seoDescription: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, killed at least four and prompted a U.S. emergency exchange of up to four million barrels of oil.
deck: The storm came ashore as a Category 2 hurricane, left about 670,000 customers without power and kept most U.S. Gulf oil output shut.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, at 8:30 p.m. Central time on October 9 with maximum sustained winds near 105 mph before rapidly weakening over Alabama, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.
At least four deaths were linked to the storm. About 670,000 customers in Florida, Alabama, Georgia and Mississippi remained without power at midday October 10, Reuters reported.

sections.heading: Energy disruption
paragraphs: About 69% of U.S. Gulf oil production and 57% of natural-gas production remained shut on October 10. Shell and Chevron began returning crews, but full restoration depended on inspections and safe operating conditions.

The U.S. Department of Energy authorized emergency exchanges of up to four million barrels of crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, split between ExxonMobil and BP America, to support refinery supply. The companies must return the borrowed oil with additional premium barrels in 2027.

sections.heading: Why it matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Disruptions to Gulf production and U.S. refinery supply can add volatility to world fuel markets. For the import-dependent Philippines, sustained price pressure can feed into pump prices, transport costs and inflation even when the storm itself is far away.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the pace of power restoration, remaining flood and tornado risks, the restart of Gulf production and refineries, and whether the emergency oil exchanges are sufficient to prevent wider supply disruption.

audit.verificationNotes: NHC confirms the landfall, intensity and rapid weakening. The U.S. Energy Department confirms the four-million-barrel emergency exchange. Reuters and AP independently corroborate the deaths, outages and damage. Death and outage counts are presented as reported totals at the stated cutoff.
audit.duplicateCheck: Landfall deaths, widespread outages and the emergency oil exchange are independently newsworthy developments after FMB’s October 8 pre-landfall shutdown report.
